editorial.headline: Tea Cultivation With a Clean National and Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: Tea farming is open across business scales, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali moratorium block under this record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01272 is the activity code for tea cultivation as an integrated agricultural operation. Its scope is not limited to the visible moment of harvest. The record covers land preparation, sowing, nursery work, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and postharvest activity when these are carried out as one chain. It also includes the planting of tea plants to produce seed in the form of beans, and expressly names nursery and seed activities for beverage crops, including tea seed production.

That matters because this is a cultivation code, not a loose label for trading tea or presenting a tea brand. The centre of gravity is the agricultural life cycle of the tea plant itself: preparing the land, raising seedlings, managing the crop, and bringing the harvest through postharvest steps that remain part of the same farming sequence. A founder using this code should therefore see it as a field-level operating category for tea plantations or tea-growing ventures, including the upstream seed and nursery work described in the record.

On scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so the classification is not confined to either smallholder activity or large estates. Nationally, the investment reading is also clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the stated foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain English, the national rule set in this record does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership. There is no basis here to invent a lower threshold, a phased timeline, or a special capital condition; the only ownership number given is the full 100% ceiling.

The Bali picture is equally important, but it should be read precisely. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province. This record, however, is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore clean: a foreign-owned tea cultivation setup is nationally open, and this record does not show a Bali PMA moratorium block. The caveat is not a hidden prohibition; it is the risk-status distinction stated in the record.
